text:
English construction: Open conditional
Example: “If the river rises, we will use the upper bridge.”
The if-clause presents a possible condition and the main clause its consequence.

text:
English construction: Remote conditional
Example: “If the river were lower, we could cross here.”
Were marks a hypothetical present condition; could describes the ability to cross under that condition. These forms do not refer to past time here.

English construction: Past counterfactual
Example: “If we had left earlier, we would have caught the ferry.”
The form imagines an alternative to an already completed past.

English construction: Unless clause
Example: “We will camp here unless the wind strengthens.”
Unless introduces an exception to the proposed course.
